items.title: Larry Ellison Ends Plan to Sell Up to $7.5 Billion in Oracle Stock
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>Oracle Corp. Chairman Larry Ellison canceled his plan to sell as many as 50 million shares in the tech company, a holding worth $7.5 billion, a day after the company disclosed the founder’s divestment plan.</article>

items.title: Amodei, Altman, Musk Call for Slowing Development of AI Models
items.author: Kevin Whitelaw and Seth Fiegerman
items.content: <article>Leaders of the world’s biggest artificial intelligence platforms said it’s time to slow the development pace of their most advanced — and most lucrative — models, citing escalating risks of the technology.</article>

items.title: Trump Brushes Off AI Doomsaying to Guard US Lead Over China
items.author: Maggie Eastland and Courtney Subramanian
items.content: <article>In June 2024, during a campaign stop in Las Vegas, then-candidate Donald Trump got a glimpse of the technology that would come to define his second presidential term.</article>

items.title: China’s AI Industry Pivots to Agents From Models, Report Says
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s artificial intelligence industry is shifting from competition in large models and computing power toward the deployment and commercialization of AI agents, according to a report by the China Telecom Research Institute cited by China Central Television on Saturday.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Mulls $10 Billion Anthropic IPO Backing, Reuters Says
items.author: Yi Wei Wong
items.content: <article>Nvidia Corp. is considering investing as much as $10 billion in Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering, which could become the biggest IPO of all time, Reuters reported.</article>

items.title: Larry Ellison Steps Back From Oracle Limelight in AI Era
items.author: Brody Ford and Edwina Otira
items.content: <article>Oracle Corp. earnings calls this year have been missing a familiar voice: Larry Ellison’s.</article>

items.title: Oracle Boosts Layoffs Plan by $700 Million
items.author: Brody Ford
items.content: <article>Oracle Corp. increased the scale of its planned job cuts while the company grapples with a cash crunch tied to development of large-scale data centers for artificial intelligence work.</article>

items.title: Russia Takes Steps to Create a Space Council With BRICS Partners
items.author: Ilya Arkhipov
items.content: <article>Russia and its partners in the BRICS group of countries are moving toward creating a council to coordinate cooperation in space, Roscosmos chief Dmitry Bakanov said in an interview in New Delhi.</article>

items.title: Kalshi Moves to Expand Into US Stock and Commodity Markets
items.author: Katherine Doherty
items.content: <article>Kalshi Inc. is filing for regulatory approval to offer the first single-stock perpetual futures in the US and is looking to expand the contracts in commodities to include agriculture, said Tarek Mansour, the company’s co-founder.</article>

items.title: Why Bridgewater’s CIO Says AI’s Human Extinction Risk Is Real
items.content:
<article>As one of the earliest backers of both OpenAI and Anthropic, Greg Jensen has seen AI development up close. Now, he's among the tech insiders more worried than ever about AI's human extinction risks.

The managing CIO of Bridgewater joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss how AI discourse is starting to resemble the start of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 and why the time for governments to put meaningful regulations in place is now. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Ally Says US Underestimates China Tech Sector After Visits
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>US Senator Steve Daines said the US may be misjudging the sophistication of China’s technology sector.</article>

items.title: Apple’s Always-Listening Watch AI Tool Could Pose Legal Risks for Users
items.author: Natalie Lung
items.content: <article>Apple Inc.’s new always-listening artificial intelligence features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 could put eavesdropping laws to the test, according to legal experts.</article>
